assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's single curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read in full with its front matter: the canonical v1.0 standalone literary monograph SHIBOYUGI_HAKUSHI_MONOGRAPH.md (SBY-P007), repository analysis of the admitted Japanese main narratives and original visual layers of SBY-JP-V01-W01 through SBY-JP-V10-W01, located by spine member and paragraph, with route evidence from V01, V03-V06 and V08-V10. The project entrypoint and the reconstruction readiness report were read only as method context and calibration. The readiness report's private bounded candidate model for Hakushi (retired, at the bar reunion and the Snow Room test), its retrospective checks, and the volume readings, ledgers and audits the monograph links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Hakushi across V01-V10 in story order rather than disclosure order: the active practitioner at Yūki's game #3 (Hormone Town, disclosed V05) and the training that follows; Candle Woods and her retirement (V01, the directly shown ninety-sixth outing); the retired woman at the magic bar after the Etsusei encounter (V03, where Yūki first learns she survived) and her later advice (V05); the private Snow Room mock game (V06); roughly two and a half years of retirement research and the direct meeting with Kūron (V08-V09); and V10, where she appears only as a precedent in other people's decisions. The active and retired states are separate capability states: her body is extensively modified after games #83 and #90, and she no longer enters lethal games. The boundary limits evidence, not her knowledge: her early life and the contents of her institutional research belong to her at every state they predate, but the source withholds most of them.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph states one mechanism and follows it through every located state: Hakushi learns by looking for what could make competence fail, and applies that scrutiny to her body (preparation before Candle Woods), to rules (the folk-tale reading, expressly delivered rules against likely equipment), to pupils (recording every game, catching small flaws) and, after retirement, to the institution (V08 S22, V09 S24). It pairs that with care that accepts release: she hopes a pupil reaches ninety-nine and accepts that the pupil may stop (V03 S23). Not B: the monograph says no statement explains all of her interest in Yūki, and whether residual attachment explains her inquiry survives Kūron's rival reading and her reply, so the account does not say which motive decides when protecting a pupil and leaving the pupil free compete. Not D: the mechanism recurs with located episodes in V01, V03, V05, V06, V08 and V09, and the account predicts her errors.

The states are located and their transitions are given reasons: an early disregard for her own death that she says changed (V05 S16); the active teacher; retirement after Kyara's performance makes her judge that her body and readiness have reached a limit (V01 S15/S17); bodily deterioration traced to games #83 and #90 and to prostheses (V03 S23, V09 S24); the retired investigator who says having time made her earlier life's context worth knowing (V08 S22). Not B: the sampled states are few and far apart, the onset of her anger and her early circumstances are undated, and V10 gives no state of her own, only others' comparisons. Not D: each state carries located evidence, and the reasons for the two main transitions are stated in the source.

Written Japanese register is analyzed by audience: 私 and お前 with pupils; 名前を教えろ and 私の弟子にしてやろう as assumed authority at #3; 外野の評価なんざ、気にするな as a terse order that loosens dependence; きさま and 臆病者 with Koyomi beside private respect; ごきげんよう to Kūron and sustained politeness toward the senior Rinrin; さあな as evasion; 私が望むのは真実だけだ as a condition for belief; 私は引退だ at exit; 女の勘 as generational marking (V01 S15/S17, V03 S23, V05 S16, V06 S20, V08 S22). Not B: about a dozen forms in five relationships, no general politeness rule, and the only audible description is Yūki's report of a low, soft, carrying voice at Candle Woods. Not D: each form is tied to a recipient and a function.

Only local items: she goes to the magic bar often enough to be familiar there, orders a drink she guides without feeling its temperature, pays for Yūki's drink, considers a friend's retirement, advises Koyomi on money and declines to watch a private recording (V03 S23, V08 S18, V09 S24). The monograph itself says food, family history, romantic attachment and experience beyond these glimpses are open. Not D: the items come from a few scenes in one setting, with no account of ordinary choices.

Her stance changes by partner, and the monograph gives some of the reasons. Yūki moves from captive novice to chosen pupil to a former pupil she releases from outside evaluation while still calling her an idiot and hoping for her success (V05 S16, V03 S23). Etsusei, another former pupil, imitates one extraordinary result, which Hakushi distinguishes from the discipline. Koyomi gets insults and private respect for a strength unlike hers. Kūron gets formal greeting, barbs and a serious appointment. The unknown senior Rinrin gets politeness and amusement. Setsuna is drawn to the microphone as a source (V06 S20). Not B: most partners appear in one or two scenes, and what decides how far she intervenes with a pupil is left open. Not D: the variables (the pupil's independent judgment, a partner's different competence, institutional standing, verification) are explicit and located.

Her interior reaches the reader mainly through her own located statements: that she once did not care whether she died; that she did not at first find the novice's likely death particularly objectionable; that finding something to do calmed her anger, as Yūki remembers it; that she meant to entrust her aim to Yūki and was surprised by how explicitly Yūki took it up; that time made the institution worth knowing (V05 S16, V04 S21, V08 S22). The narrator represents a pause and a choice of words at #3. Not C: the monograph treats these as windows into chosen practical reasons and retrospective distance, says none explains all of her interest in Yūki, and leaves whether attachment drives the inquiry open. Not E: several self-accounts are located across states and kept separate from other characters' readings.

Contest and argument method is located: at #3 she uses the available margin and infers novice status from a slip about a civil name; at Candle Woods she tests how an opponent can misread a corpse and leaves a concealed weapon for Yūki as entrustment with real cost (V01 S15/S17); in the Snow Room she infers her opponent from personal knowledge and duplicate settings, keeps talking to draw Setsuna out, weighs the risk that winning her safer side costs Yūki the dangerous side, solves the last puzzle and still falls through a separate trap she overlooked (V06 S20); she calls Kūron's interpretation badly wrong and trades barbs (V09 S24). The account predicts her mistakes: concentration on a plausible rule that misses a machine's actual effect, and banter to protect herself afterward. Not B: few contests are sampled, and the row and the monograph leave her thresholds for preparation, physical intervention or withdrawal in a novel present-day emergency open. Not D: the method and its failure mode recur across V01, V05 and V06.

The discovery row does not claim ETHICS, and the monograph does not analyze ethical reasoning as such. Its nearby material (declining to name a deserving survivor between Yūki and Etsusei, recasting help as a way to stay alive long enough for a choice) is used under psychology and relationships, not graded here.

Only local items: the 臆病者 jab at Koyomi, amusement at the abrasive senior Rinrin, and the banter with which she covers a mistake after the Snow Room test (V03 S23, V06 S20/S22). Not D: the monograph treats the banter as self-protection after error, not as an analyzed pattern of play.

The portrait routes every material claim to spine and paragraph locators across her appearances in V01, V03-V06 and V08-V10, separates late-disclosed actions and later reports as distinct kinds of evidence, and preserves an unresolved source contradiction (the directly shown ninety-sixth outing in V01 against ninety-five in V03, V06, V08 and the V09 plate) instead of reconciling it. The project routes it complete at the V10 boundary. Not A: it is one literary portrait with no curated model, ledger or check on this subject, and the source itself withholds the contents of her research. Not C: coverage of her appearances is complete for the declared boundary.

Affirmative evidence of her limits and mistakes: her first declaration at #3 barely treats Yūki as a chooser until Yūki objects; her phantom hypothesis in the Snow Room has the wrong person for one appearance; she overlooks the separate trap; her story of deliberately surrendering the advantage is inconsistent with her own reasoning while falling, and she acknowledges the error when Yūki questions it; Koyomi's refusal of even an alternative investment checks the range of her advice; her claims about present capacity must answer to performance (V05 S16, V06 S20/S22, V03 S23). Not A: the evidence does not explain the gaps it marks. Not C: these are located findings, not inferences from silence.

Claims are placed by volume, spine and paragraph, story order is separated from disclosure order (#3 shown in V05; her survival disclosed in V03 after the reader saw it in V01), and the monograph keeps what Yūki knows at each point apart from what the reader knows. The retirement span is given as roughly two and a half years by her own account and narration. Not A: her early experiences are undated and some states are given by period (after #83 and #90) rather than a located boundary. Not C: the active and retired states and the bodily thresholds are located.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation.

Register limited to the sampled relationships: a pupil or former pupil (Yūki), a long-standing drinking companion (Koyomi), the head of the game organization (Kūron), and the senior Rinrin, an older organizer of the Snow Room mock game whom she meets there for the first time and who sets up its separate trigger (V06 S20).
No spoken voice beyond the one reported description, no extended casual conversation, and no intimate or romantic register.
scenario_readiness.note: The audience-conditioned forms constrain short written lines in the sampled relationships enough for illustrative use. Not READY: about a dozen located forms and no general register rule. Not NOT_READY: the forms are tied to recipient and function across several scenes.

conditions: Source-near counterfactuals that change one located element (a rule, an offer of information, a pupil's choice) and state the change.

Predict her method at moderate confidence: look for what an apparent rule omits; trust information more when she can check it; give a pupil specific criticism and alternatives without promising to shield the pupil from a choice; voice hope while leaving the choice to the other person.
Include her predicted errors: fixing on a plausible rule and missing a separate mechanism, and covering a mistake with banter until questioned.
Give how far she would intervene for a pupil, and any physical intervention or withdrawal in a novel emergency, only as alternatives, never as a single prediction.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Retired Hakushi between the V03 bar reunion and the V09 meeting with Kūron, with her modified body and no longer entering lethal games; she knows Yūki is alive and training, and she knows what V03-V09 show her learning, not the withheld contents of her research.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Yūki as a former pupil she has released, Koyomi as a long-standing companion, an institutional figure offering information, an opponent she cannot at first identify in a mock game, or a senior organizer of such a game (Rinrin, met there for the first time). Etsusei and Setsuna are sampled only once each; any comparable former pupil is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: The magic bar or a comparable private advisory conversation, a mock contest run by the same operators that is relatively safe on her side (substitute penalties, though a separate physical hazard can still reach her), with the other player's side and its danger stated separately and not assumed to be low, or a direct inquiry meeting.
No lethal game with her as a participant after retirement, no cross-series setting, no life after V10, and no change to the industry's rules without a stated assumption.

scenario_readiness.note: The failure-seeking method, the verification condition and the release-with-hope pattern support narrow extrapolation near the sampled scenes. Not READY: what decides between protecting and releasing a pupil, and her emergency thresholds, are open. Not NOT_READY: the method and its predicted errors recur with located outcomes.

conditions: Only the sampled bar conversations with Koyomi or Yūki: drinks, teasing, advice and paying.
No daily routine, food, family, home life or affect beyond the located items.
scenario_readiness.note: Not READY: ordinary life is a few glimpses in one setting, and the monograph lists food, family and romance as open. Not NOT_READY: the bar conversations are located twice with consistent conduct.
Not assessed: the row does not claim ETHICS, and the monograph gives no analyzed ethical reasoning to test a scenario against.

The monograph states that her condition does not settle romantic life and lists a romantic attachment among what is open. Nothing supports reconstructing her with a partner. This bounds use and is not a finding of incapacity.

conditions: Supported: her teaching practice (recording each game, building usable knowledge across problem types, catching small flaws), preparation before a contest, reading rules against likely equipment, entrustment to a pupil, and the retired investigator's demand for checkable information.
Active-practitioner conduct is limited to the #3 and Candle Woods states; retired conduct to advice, the mock game and the Kūron meeting.
Not supported: her conduct in a full lethal game after retirement, the contents or conclusions of her research beyond what V08-V09 show, and any judgment of hers on Yūki's V10 treatment.
scenario_readiness.note: This is her best-sampled domain. Not READY: emergency thresholds and the motive behind her inquiry are open. Not NOT_READY: method, mentoring and verification are located across V01-V09.

known_limits.statement: The monograph says no statement explains all of Hakushi's interest in Yūki, and whether residual attachment explains her institutional inquiry survives Kūron's rival reading (suicidal risk disguised as investigation) and her rejection of it. A model cannot say which motive decides when protecting and releasing a pupil compete.

The directly shown V01 exit is her ninety-sixth outing, while V03, V06, V08 and the V09 plate give ninety-five. The source supplies no bookkeeping rule that reconciles them, so a model must not state one count as settled.
Narration credits her with learning the organization's story and withholds most of what she found; the Wall of Thirty data and method do not reach the reader. A model must not invent her findings.

Retired Hakushi has extensively modified organs and prostheses, cannot feel temperature in her fingers, and was badly hurt at #83 and #90. The design and provider of each alteration are uncertain, and her statements about present capacity answer to performance. Active-state capability does not transfer to the retired state.

The bar conversation releases one authority claim over Yūki; it does not end either woman's ability to affect the other, and she still intervenes closely when another person's apparent lack of a future matters to her.
At V10 she appears only as a precedent in other people's decisions and comparisons; how she continued after serious injury is not her judgment about Yūki's hospital treatment.
Her thresholds for preparation, physical intervention or withdrawal in a novel present-day emergency are not established.
Food, family history, romantic attachment, daily routine and experience beyond the story's few glimpses are not evidenced.
Only written Japanese register and one reported description of her voice are available; pitch, accent and extended ordinary conversation are not evidenced.

The curated evidence is one compact literary monograph over a small number of located scenes; no operational model, decision ledger or model check is curated on this subject, so the narrow conditional predictions rest on one line of evidence.
